summary: Static-only verification (no runtime/DB, per environment constraints) of iteration-3 fixes: category/tags support in updateOfferControlsImpl + its Zod schema, pagination of the manual-flag lookup in syncProviderImpl, and the two stale comments (toRow + migration 20261125000000 header). All 7 requested review bullets PASS. Extended the previous static pytest suite from 14 to 22 tests (2 stale assertions referencing removed variables were updated; 8 new tests added for the new behaviour). Result: 22/22 PASS.

minor.issue: Server-side write path for category/tags on network offers now exists, but the admin UI still cannot reach it: controlsAction's mutationFn input type has no category/tags, and the network-offer row only renders reward/payout-mode controls (category+tags editor lives solely in the manual-offer dialog, and openEdit/Edit button is rendered only for source !== 'network'). So the *_manual flags still cannot be set for network offers from the UI — only via a direct server-fn/API call. Original HIGH concern (a) is resolved at the API layer only.

toRow never emits a `tags` key, so `delete row['tags']` when tags_manual is true is a permanent no-op. Harmless today (sync never overwrites tags) but the tags_manual branch is dead code and could mislead future changes; consider a comment or removal.

Unbounded `for (let from = 0; ; from += PAGE_SIZE)` has no hard iteration ceiling. Correct given PostgREST returns a short final page, but a defensive max-pages guard would prevent an infinite loop if the backend ever returns a full page repeatedly.

action_items: Optional (completes original HIGH item a): add category/tags to OffersManager's controlsAction input type and expose a category select + tag toggles for network offers so admins can actually set the *_manual flags from the UI.
Optional: document or remove the dead `delete row['tags']` branch in sync.server.ts since toRow never writes `tags`.
Optional: add a max-page guard to the manual-flag pagination loop.
critical_code_review_comments: updateOfferControlsImpl: category/tags are added to the patch only under `!== undefined` guards and each flips its matching *_manual flag to true — verified correct, and `category: null` (explicit clear) still flips category_manual, which is the intended semantic.
Zod schema for updateOfferControls: category enum matches the SQL CHECK constraint values exactly; tags capped at 4 (max 4 distinct values). All pre-existing fields intact.

Pagination: PAGE_SIZE=1000 with .range(from, from + PAGE_SIZE - 1), single Map declared outside the loop, `if (pageError) throw pageError` aborts the sync (caught by outer try/catch which sets provider sync_status='error' and rethrows), and loop breaks on a short page. Semantics (provider_id filter, delete of locked columns, upsert of mutated rows) preserved.

Migration 20261125000000: body contains only the two idempotent DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS / DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS statements; no CREATE TRIGGER/FUNCTION anywhere. Header and toRow comments now describe the sync-engine strip pattern referencing syncProviderImpl.

Grep across /app/src and /app/supabase: the only remaining mentions of preserve_offer_admin_overrides / preserve_manual_offer_overrides are the DROP statements plus explanatory comments inside migrations 20261125000000 and 20261126000000.
context_for_next_testing_agent: No node_modules / no live Supabase; all verification is static (regex/grep + pytest at /app/tests/test_offer_manual_override_static.py, now 22 tests). Iteration-3 spec items are fully implemented. Only remaining gap is UI-level: OffersManager has no category/tags controls for network offers, so *_manual flags are unsettable from the admin UI even though the server fn accepts them. If the main agent adds that UI, re-verify the controlsAction input type + a data-testid on the new network-offer category select/tag toggles.
rca_of_the_issue: Two of the previous suite's 14 assertions failed only because the refactor renamed the flag-query variables (existingError -> pageError, inline Map construction -> manualFlags.set inside the paging loop). These were stale test assertions, not product defects; updated in place and the suite now passes 22/22.
